query: Most of my money is in cash right now. Is that okay or should I shift it into investments?

recommendations.title: Maintain High Cash Position for Emergency Fund
recommendations.summary: Keep majority of cash reserves intact to complete your critical emergency fund goal before increasing investment exposure.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $15,000 in cash and no emergency fund established, you're actually in a prudent position. Your emergency fund target is $22,000 (6 months of expenses at $3,800/month). You need approximately $7,000 more to reach this goal. Given your conservative risk tolerance (loss comfort 3/10), moderate debt ($38,000), and beginner experience, maintaining this cash position is appropriate. The psychological and financial security of a complete emergency fund outweighs potential investment returns, especially in your current negative net worth situation. Once emergency fund is complete, you can gradually shift excess cash to investments.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current $15,000 cash position and continue contributing to reach $22,000 emergency fund target

recommendations.title: Accelerate Emergency Fund Completion
recommendations.summary: Prioritize directing monthly surplus toward completing emergency fund in next 6-12 months before considering additional investments.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your monthly income ($6,000) minus expenses ($3,800) leaves approximately $2,200 surplus. After accounting for debt payments, you likely have $500-1,000 available monthly. Direct 100% of available surplus to high-yield savings account (currently offering 4.0-5.0% APY) to complete the remaining $7,000 emergency fund gap. This could be achieved in 7-14 months. This recommendation aligns with your high-priority emergency goal and conservative risk profile. Only after this foundation is secure should you increase investment allocations. Consider opening accounts like Marcus, Ally, or Wealthfront Cash for better returns than traditional savings.
recommendations.suggested_action: Open high-yield savings account and direct monthly surplus to reach $22,000 emergency fund target

recommendations.title: Maintain Conservative Investment Mix
recommendations.summary: Current 40% investment allocation (30% VTTSX, 10% BND) is appropriate for your risk profile and should remain unchanged until emergency fund is complete.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your existing investments totaling $10,000 represent a balanced approach for a beginner with conservative risk tolerance. VTTSX (Vanguard Target Retirement fund) provides automatic diversification and age-appropriate asset allocation, while BND (Vanguard Total Bond Market) adds stability. This 30/10 split in stocks/bonds is conservative and suitable given your negative net worth and moderate debt. Do not liquidate these positions or add new investment capital until your emergency fund is fully funded. These holdings are already working toward your medium-term house down payment goal (5-7 years), which aligns with the VTTSX time horizon.
recommendations.suggested_action: Continue holding existing positions without additional contributions until emergency fund complete

recommendations.title: Address Debt Alongside Savings Strategy
recommendations.summary: Evaluate debt interest rates and consider balanced approach between emergency fund completion and high-interest debt reduction.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $38,000 in liabilities creating a negative net worth of $13,000, debt interest costs may be eroding your financial progress. If carrying high-interest debt (credit cards >15% APR), consider a hybrid approach: direct 60-70% of surplus to emergency fund completion and 30-40% to highest-rate debt payoff. However, if debt is primarily student loans or car loans at <6%, prioritize emergency fund completion first. The security of emergency funds prevents further debt accumulation during unexpected expenses. Once emergency fund reaches $15,000-18,000 (4-5 months), you could split contributions between final emergency fund completion and aggressive debt paydown.
recommendations.suggested_action: Assess debt interest rates; if >10% APR exists, allocate 30% of monthly surplus to highest-rate debt while building emergency fund
